Nothing in this subsection shall prohibit a retail consumption dealer or retail package dealer from catering or supplying a private party or gathering being put on by a third party at a location other than that covered by the license.
(b) For a retail consumption dealer, if the sale of alcoholic beverages within an establishment or business at a specific location is handled through a concession contract, the license for such location shall be obtained jointly in the name of the entity which operates the business or establishment within which such concession is located and the name of the entity operating the concession. The term "concession contract," for the purposes of this subsection, means an agreement or arrangement where the person selling alcoholic beverages is doing so as a department or section of a larger business enterprise, for example, a beverage service operated within a hotel, food and beverage services operated within an indoor commercial recreational establishment or outdoor commercial recreational establishment, or a beverage service operated within an eating establishment. For the purposes of determining whether a particular business enterprise qualifies as an eating establishment, hotel, indoor commercial recreational establishment or an outdoor commercial recreational establishment, the activities, facilities and sales of the business enterprise as a whole shall be aggregated, and the individual sales or facilities of any concession therein shall not be treated separately.
(Code 2012, § 3-147; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
159:
(a) A person desiring to obtain a license under this article shall make application to the city clerk on the forms prescribed by the city clerk.
(b) The application shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
(1) The name and address of the applicant and the proposed business to be carried on;
(2) If a partnership, the names and residence addresses of all of the partners unless there are more than twenty (20) partners, in which case the application shall list all partners having, directly or indirectly, at least a five-percent interest in the assets or revenues of the partnership;
(3) If a corporation, the names and residence addresses of the officers, the directors, the registered agent for service of process, the manager of the business for which the license is sought and all shareholders unless there are more than twenty (20) shareholders, in which case the application shall list all shareholders holding at least five (5) percent of the capital stock of the corporation; and
(4) If a private club, the names and residence addresses of the officers, directors and the manager of such private club.
(c) All applicants shall furnish data, fingerprints, evidence of financial responsibility in the form of a bond in the amount of one million dollars ($1,000,000.00) or insurance with a minimum coverage of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000.00) per person and five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000.00) per incident, a copy of the current city business license for the establishment, certification from the tax commissioner that all taxes due to the city and county by the applicant have been paid and other material as required by the city clerk. Failure to furnish such data as required by the city clerk shall be deemed to be a withdrawal of the application.
(d) Each application for an initial license as opposed to a license renewal shall have attached thereto a plat of the land on which the establishment is proposed to be located showing the location of the improvements thereon. Such plat must be prepared by a land surveyor registered under the laws of the state and the surveyor shall show on the plat and certify as to the accuracy thereof the distance from the main entrance door of the proposed establishment to any school building, church building, city park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility located within five hundred (500) yards thereof measured under the applicable provisions of section 3-152.
(e) All applications shall be sworn to by the applicant before a notary public or other officer empowered by law to administer oaths.
(f) An application shall be presented to the city council or a committee designated by the city council within forty-five (45) days after the date such application is deemed complete by the city clerk. The city clerk shall notify the applicant in writing of the date on which the application will be presented to the city council or its designated committee, which notice shall be given in sufficient time to enable the applicant to meet the public notice requirements as set forth in section 3-151.
(g) At the time the application is presented to the city council or its designated committee, the applicant may appear and present any matters in support of the application and any other person may appear and present matters in opposition to the application. Upon hearing all of the presentations, the city council or its designated committee shall take action denying or granting the application or deferring action for a period not to exceed forty-five (45) days in order to obtain further information. If the application is denied, the city council or its designated committee shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for the denial.
(h) In all instances in which an application is denied under the provisions of this article, the applicant may not reapply for a similar license for the same location for at least one (1) year from the date of such denial.
(Code 2012, § 3-148; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
160:
Any application for a license made pursuant to this article may be withdrawn by the applicant at any time. If the application is withdrawn before the license is issued, any sums deposited as license fees will be refunded. After issuance of a license, no refunds will be made. No refunds shall be made under any circumstances for investigation and administrative fees required in this article.
(Code 2012, § 3-149; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
161:
(a) A license under this article will be issued only to a person who is a citizen of the United States or an alien lawfully admitted for permanent residence in the United States. Where an applicant is other than a natural person, such applicant must be an entity organized and existing under the laws of the United States or one (1) of its states, and the natural persons who are required to join in the application must meet the qualifications of this subsection.
(b) For a license to be issued to a general partnership, the application must be made jointly by the partnership, any managing partner and all other partners owning at least a twenty (20) percent interest in the assets or revenues of the partnership. If there is no managing partner, nor a partner meeting the ownership requirements, the application then must be made jointly in the name of the partnership and the general partner owning the greatest percentage interest in the assets and revenues of the partnership. At least one (1) of the applicants shall be a natural person. If none of the applicants required in this subsection is a natural person, then the natural person having primary responsibility for the operation of the business for which the license is sought shall join in the application.
(c) Where the applicant for a license is a limited partnership, the application shall be made jointly by the limited partnership, its general partner and any other partner, limited or general, owning at least a twenty (20) percent interest in the assets or revenues of the limited partnership. At least one (1) of the applicants must be a natural person. If none of the applicants required in this subsection is a natural person, then the natural person having primary responsibility for the operation of the business for which the license is sought shall join in the application.
(d) Where the applicant for a license is a corporation, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the corporation and its president or vice-president and any stockholder owning at least twenty (20) percent of the total outstanding capital stock of the corporation.
(e) Where the applicant for a license is a private club, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the private club and its president or general manager.
(f) Where the applicant for a license is an entity other than a natural person, partnership, corporation or private club, the application shall be made jointly in the name of the entity, the natural person having chief executive officer authority over the business activities of the entity and any other person having at least a five (5) percent interest in the assets or revenues of the entity. The application shall further disclose the type of entity making the application and every person having an ownership interest in the assets or revenues of the entity.
(g) Licenses issued to corporations, general partnerships, limited partnerships, private clubs or other types of entities must be issued jointly to the entity and all of the other persons required by this section to join in the application.
(h) No person shall be granted a license unless it shall appear to the satisfaction of the city council or its designated committee that such person shall be of good moral character or, in the case of an entity which is not a natural person, that such entity has a good reputation, and in no event shall a license be granted to any person who has been convicted or has pled guilty or entered a plea of nolo contendere to any charge involving a crime of moral turpitude, gambling or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or illegal possession of alcoholic beverages within a period of ten (10) years immediately prior to the filing of such application. In the case of a partnership, corporation, private club or other business entity, a license shall not be issued to the partnership, corporation, private club or other entity if any partner, officer, director, shareholder or other person required to be listed on the application, even if such person is not required to be a joint applicant, cannot meet the requirements as set forth in this subsection in the same manner as though such individual was the applicant. At the time an application is submitted for a license, the applicant shall, by a duly sworn affidavit, certify that all of the requirements of this section have been met by the applicant and the other persons required to be listed on the application as set forth in this subsection. Should any person in whose name a license is issued or any person whose name is required to be listed on the application for a license under this article, after the license has been issued, be convicted or plead guilty or nolo contendere to a charge involving a crime of moral turpitude, gambling or illegal possession or sale of controlled substances or illegal possession of alcoholic beverages, the license shall be immediately revoked and cancelled.
(i) No license under this article shall be issued to any person convicted or pleading guilty or nolo contendere to any charge under any federal, state or local law constituting a felony within ten (10) years prior to the date of the filing of the application for such license.
(j) No license under this article shall be issued to any person who has had any license issued under the police powers of any city or county revoked within two (2) years prior to the filing of the application for a license under this article.
(k) The city council or its designated committee may decline to issue a license under this article when any person having any ownership interest in or control over the land or building in which the establishment to be operated pursuant to the license will be located does not meet the same character requirements as set forth in this section for the licensee.
(l) If a person in whose name a license under this article is issued is not a county resident, such person must appoint and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this article may be served. The registered agent must be a resident of the county. If the licensee is not a natural person, it will be required to appoint and maintain a registered agent in the county if it does not have in the county any agent upon whom process can legally be served for such entity under the laws of the state. The licensee shall file the name of such registered agent, along with the written consent to serve of such agent, with the city clerk.
(m) An application for a license under this article may be denied where it appears to the city council or its designated committee that the applicant does not have adequate financial strength, adequate financial participation in the proposed business to direct and manage its affairs, or where it appears that the applicant is intended or is likely to be a surrogate for a person who would not otherwise qualify for a license under this article.
(n) The city council or its designated committee, in its discretion, may consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, the application or the proposed location of the establishment. If, in the city council's or the committee's judgment, circumstances are such that issuing of a license under this article would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.
(Code 2012, § 3-150; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
162:
A person filing an application for a new license under this article, as opposed to an application for the renewal of an existing license, shall give public notice of the filing of the application as follows:
(1) By publishing a notice of the application in the newspaper in which sheriff's sales in the county are placed, in a form approved by the city clerk, three (3) times in the thirty (30) days preceding the consideration of the application by the city council;
(2) By posting a sign for at least thirty (30) days preceding the consideration of the application by the city council in a prominent position on the property where it can be readily read from the road, which states:
"Application has been made to the city council for a license to sell (beer) (wine) (distilled spirits) for consumption (on) (off) premises at this location."
Date: _____ | Name of Applicant: _____
The applicant must provide the city council proof of the giving of such public notice at or prior to the city council's consideration of the application.
(Code 2012, § 3-151; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
163:
(a) No establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article shall be located in a building which is closer than one hundred (100) yards to a church building, library, day care, children's nursery, or an alcoholic treatment facility, or closer than two hundred (200) yards to a school building. In applying this section, the city council shall determine what property is included in a school building, church building, city park or playground, or alcoholic treatment facility consistent with the definitions set forth in section 3-102, and the determination of the city council shall be final.
(b) For the purposes of this section, subject to the qualifications set forth in this subsection, distances shall be measured in a straight line from the main entrance door of the establishment for which the license under this article is being sought to the nearest point on the boundary line of the land making up the campus of the church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility. All lots and parcels of land bordering on Wrightsboro Road at the edge of the city limits up to and including the intersection of Wrightsboro Road and Robinson Avenue is hereby declared to be a "special commercial growth center" only for the purposes of complying with this article. As such all distances from any church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility which is built, acquired or established after December 31, 2002, or in the case of areas added to the designated areas which are built, acquired or established after the effective date of such designation, distance shall be measured from the main entrance door of the establishment for which a license is being sought to the nearest point of the centerline of the nearest traveled road, street or highway, then measured along such centerline to a point on the centerline nearest the main entrance door of the school building, church building, or alcoholic treatment facility and then measured in a straight line from such centerline to such main entrance door. If any church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility located in one (1) of the designated areas on December 31, 2002, or the effective date of designation of an area added to the designated areas after December 31, 2002, as the case may be, thereafter has added to its campus additional land, measurement of the distance requirements shall continue to be made as provided in the first sentence of this subsection (b), but the land acquired after December 31, 2002, or the effective designation date, as the case may be, shall not be considered to be part of the land or campus of the church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility.
(c) No establishment which is being operated pursuant to a city license to sell beer and/or wine on January 1, 2003, the effective date of this article, shall be denied continued operation under such existing license, nor denied any renewal of such license, nor shall any new owner of such establishment be denied a new license based upon the measurements set forth in this section. Upon cessation of the operation of the establishment as set forth in section 3-156 pursuant to such license, such exemption shall cease.
(d) If the distance requirements in this section are met at the time of issuance of a license under this article, the subsequent opening and operation of a church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility within the distances prohibited in this section shall not prevent the continued operation of the establishment pursuant to the license or the renewal of the license or the issuance of a new license to any subsequent owner of such establishment as long as the business operation of the establishment does not cease as set forth in section 3-156.
(e) The holder of title to any property making up a church building, school building, or alcoholic treatment facility may waive the distance requirements of this section as they apply to such facility in any specific instance by recording in the real estate records in the office of the clerk of superior court of the county, a written instrument evidencing such waiver and setting out the terms thereof, which instrument shall be executed and witnessed with the same formalities as a deed filed for record in the clerk's office.
(f) Nothing in this section shall prohibit the city council from amending this section, adding additional special commercial growth centers nor amending any distance requirements in the future.
(Code 2012, § 3-152; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
164:
(a) Upon making application for a license under this article, the applicant shall pay a license fee for the license, an administrative and investigative fee and such other fees as may be established from time to time by the city council by resolution adopted in open meeting and kept on file in the office of the city clerk. The initial schedule of fees shall be adopted and is attached to the Alcoholic Beverage Control Ordinance adopted January 1, 2003. Such schedule of fees shall remain in effect until amended by the city council. All applicants shall be furnished a copy of the schedule of fees at the time of application for a license under this article. In addition, all fees and taxes due the state, city, and/or county by the applicant, or upon the property on which the establishment is to be located, must be paid in full at or prior to the time of filing the application for the license.
(b) All licenses granted under this article shall be for a calendar year and the full license fee must be paid for a license application at the time of the filing of the application.
(c) Each application for a license under this article shall be accompanied by a certified check for the full amount of the license fee, together with a separate certified check in the amount of the applicable investigate and administrative fees. If the applicant is denied a state license, the deposit representing the license fee shall be refunded, but the investigative and administrative fees shall be retained.
(Code 2012, § 3-153; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
165:
A license issued under this article shall at all times be kept plainly exposed to public view at the place of business for which the license was granted.
(Code 2012, § 3-154; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
166:
(a) No license under this article shall be transferable, except as otherwise provided in this section.
(b) In case of the death of a licensee who is the sole licensee, the establishment for which the license was issued shall be allowed to continue to sell alcoholic beverages in accordance with the terms of the license for a period of forty-five (45) days from the date of death of the licensee or until approval of a new licensee, whichever shall first occur; provided, however, that no sale of alcoholic beverages shall be allowed after the seventh day after the date of death of the licensee until such time as a personal representative of the estate of the deceased licensee, appointed by a probate court of competent jurisdiction, shall have registered with the city clerk on forms prepared by the city clerk. Such personal representative shall be subject to all of the requirements that applied to the deceased licensee, and shall agree in writing to operate the establishment during the interim period in accordance with the terms of the license and the laws of the state and city.
(c) In the case of licenses issued jointly to partnerships and certain partners, corporations and certain officers or stockholders, private clubs and certain officers or other entities and certain persons related thereto as set forth in section 3-150, if one (1) of the joint holders of such a license severs his association with the establishment operated pursuant to the license, the establishment may continue to sell alcoholic beverages for a period of forty-five (45) days from the date determined by the city clerk to be the date of severance, provided no such sale shall be authorized until such time as an application to substitute the person taking the place of the departing person as a joint holder of the license is made by the appropriate person. If the change is one which results from a change in control of the licensee, partnership, corporation or other business entity, then an application for a new license must be filed. Upon issuance of a new license, the authorization to sell under the previous license shall be revoked by operation of law.
(d) Any change in the ownership of a licensee which is not a natural person which would change the ownership information furnished on the most recently updated application for the license must be reported to the city clerk within ten (10) days following the occurrence of such change in ownership. If such change in ownership results in an additional person being required to be a joint licensee under section 3-148, or an additional person being listed on the application, but not as a joint licensee, the license may be revoked if any such person fails to meet the qualifications required by this article. If such change in ownership results in a change in control of the business entity which is a joint licensee, then a new application must be filed for the issuance of a new license. If an application for a new license is filed within seven (7) days of the date on which the change in control occurred, then the establishment may continue to operate under the old license for a period of forty-five (45) days from the date of the change in control or until the new license is issued or denied, whichever shall occur first.
(e) If substantially all of the assets of an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article are sold, conveyed or otherwise transferred by the licensee, and if an application for a new license is filed with the city clerk within seven (7) days of such sale or transfer, the establishment may continue to be operated under the then existing license for a period of forty-five (45) days or until a new license is issued or denied to the new owner, whichever shall occur first.
(f) Under no circumstances shall a license be transferred where the original holder of the license is under suspension.
(Code 2012, § 3-155; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
167:
Any licensee who shall, for a period of two (2) consecutive months after the license under this article has been issued, cease to operate the business of selling alcoholic beverages as authorized in the license shall, after the two-month period, automatically forfeit the license without the necessity of any further action. If the business operation of selling alcoholic beverages is interrupted as a result of damage to the premises which is being repaired or because the premises is being remodeled, then this section shall not apply to such cessation of operation. If a license is issued for the operation of an establishment in a building which has not yet been completed, the license will not be forfeited unless the licensee fails to begin operations within a period of one hundred eighty (180) days from the date of issuance of the license.
(Code 2012, § 3-156; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
168:
(a) All licenses granted under this article shall expire on December 31 of each year. Licensees who desire to renew their license shall file application with the city clerk on the form provided for renewal of the license for the ensuing year. Applications for renewal must be filed on or before October 31 of each year. If a renewal application is received after October 31, the city cannot assure the applicant that a renewal license will be issued by January 1 and the licensee will have to cease the sale of alcoholic beverages from January 1 until the renewal license is issued. If a license renewal application is received after December 31, such application shall be treated as an application for a new license and the applicant shall be required to comply with all rules, regulations and fees for the granting of licenses as if no previous license had been issued.
(b) Any person applying for renewal of a license must pay the license, administrative and investigative fees at the time of filing the application. Failure to pay such fees at that time shall result in the application for renewal being treated as not filed or withdrawn.
(Code 2012, § 3-157; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
169:
The city clerk, in order to determine if the provisions of this chapter are being complied with or to determine the eligibility of an applicant, may require a licensee or an applicant for a license under this article to provide the city clerk with audited financial statements of the licensee or applicant for such period as the city clerk may determine. The city clerk shall also have the authority to conduct an audit of the books and records of a licensee or an applicant. If the city clerk deems it necessary to conduct such an audit, the city clerk shall so notify the licensee or applicant of the date, time and place of the audit. The city clerk shall designate the person to perform such audit. The licensee shall cooperate with such audit or forfeit all licenses issued under this article. If an applicant for a license fails to cooperate with an audit, the application shall be deemed withdrawn.
(Code 2012, § 3-158; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
170:
If any person shall fail to pay any sum due under this chapter, the city clerk or his designee shall issue an execution against the delinquent person and his property for the amount of the delinquent fee or tax. The failure to pay any taxes or fees shall be deemed a violation of this chapter and the license of the business to sell alcohol shall be suspended immediately.
(Code 2012, § 3-159; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
171:
Each licensee shall keep a copy of this chapter, the Georgia Alcoholic Beverage Code and any regulations issued under such code on the premises. The licensee shall instruct any employee or agent of the licensee working in connection with the sale of alcoholic beverages as to the requirements of all laws and regulations applicable to such sales so that the licensee, his agents and employees selling alcoholic beverages shall at all times be familiar with the requirements of the laws and regulations applicable to such sales. The licensee shall be responsible for any acts of his agents or employees which are in violation of this chapter or of the laws of the state or the rules and regulations of the state revenue commissioner applicable to the sale of alcoholic beverages.
(Code 2012, § 3-160; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
172:
(a) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked by the city council when the licensee furnishes fraudulent or untruthful information on the application or any renewal application for a license, or for failure of the licensee to pay all fees, taxes or other charges imposed under the provisions of this chapter or other laws or ordinances of the city or state.
(b) Whenever the state shall revoke or suspend any permit or license to sell alcoholic beverages, the license issued under this article shall be automatically revoked or suspended, as the case may be.
(c) If the city clerk, the city council or its designated committee believes that probable cause exists to find that a violation of sections 3-106, 3-188 and/or 3-194 has occurred in an establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article, the city council or its designated committee may temporarily suspend such license pending final determination and action on the matter by the city council or its designated committee.
(d) The city clerk shall revoke all of the licenses of any licensee under this article who has had three or more suspensions or revocations of a license, including all of his licenses in any consecutive 36-month period.
(e) The city clerk shall revoke a license under this article where alcoholic beverages have been sold or distributed at the location covered by the license during a period of suspension of such license.
(f) The city council may suspend or revoke any license under this article when the licensee does not meet the licensing qualifications set forth in this article and such information becomes known to the city clerk or the city council.
(g) An act or omission of a licensee under this article, by the owner of a twenty (20) percent or more interest in an establishment operated pursuant to a license, the manager of an establishment operated pursuant to a license or an employee of the establishment operated pursuant to a license working in some aspect of the sale of alcoholic beverages who willingly or knowingly performed any act, which constitutes a violation of federal or state law or this chapter will subject the licensee to suspension or revocation of his license when the city council determines that the act or omission did occur, regardless of whether any criminal prosecution or conviction ensues; provided, however, that in the case of a manager or employee, the city council must determine that the acts of the manager or employee were known to or, under reasonable circumstances, should have been known to the licensee, or were condoned by the licensee, or that the licensee had not established reasonable practices or procedures to prevent such act or omission from occurring.
(h) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the city council determines that a licensee no longer maintains adequate financial strength or responsibility upon which issuance of the license was based or whenever the licensee has defaulted in any obligation of any kind whatsoever lawfully owing to the city.
(i) A license under this article may be suspended or revoked whenever the city council determines that the establishment operated pursuant to the license has been the scene of repeated incidents of violence resulting in injury to a person or damage to property or a disturbance of the peace or requiring the intervention of law enforcement officers on the scene of a single incident of severe violence resulting in the death of a person or serious injury to a person requiring inpatient hospital care for the injured person.
(j) Upon completion of any period of suspension, a license under this article shall not be reinstated until the licensee has paid the city a reinstatement fee equal to the original license fee for that calendar year. In addition, the licensee shall pay the administrative and investigative fees and update all license application forms.
(Code 2012, § 3-161; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
173:
(a) Unless otherwise provided in this chapter, or unless waived by the licensee, no license under this article shall be suspended or revoked without the opportunity for a hearing as provided in this section.
(b) The city clerk shall provide written notice to the licensee of the initiation of an action to suspend or revoke a license. Such written notification shall set forth, in reasonable detail, the reasons for such action and shall notify the licensee of the right to a hearing under the provisions of this section. Any licensee against whom action for the suspension or revocation of a license is initiated may have a hearing concerning such action before the city council or a committee thereof designated by the city council. Such hearing shall be by written request, filed in the office of the city clerk within twenty (20) days after the date of the notice of the initiation of the action from the city clerk to the licensee. Such written request shall set forth the reasons why the licensee feels that the proposed action should not be taken and, in reasonable detail, the grounds and facts which the licensee contends support the licensee's position. The city council shall determine whether or not the license shall be temporarily suspended during the period prior to the hearing and until action is taken by the city council or its designated committee. Failure of the licensee to request a hearing within the time specified shall be deemed to be a waiver by the licensee of a right to a hearing, and the city council shall be authorized to proceed with final action on the matter without the holding of a hearing.
(c) The city council, by resolution, may assign the duties of conducting a hearing to a committee of the city council. The committee's action shall be final.
(d) A hearing, if requested, shall be held within forty-five (45) days of the date of filing the request for a hearing with the city clerk. At such hearing the licensee shall have the right to be represented by an attorney, at the expense of the licensee, and to present evidence and cross-examine witnesses.
(e) The action of the city council or its committee shall be forwarded to the city clerk within fifteen (15) days after the conclusion of the hearing, and the city clerk shall notify the licensee by certified mail, return receipt requested, of the action taken by the city council or its committee.
(f) The action of the city council or its committee shall be final when taken.
(Code 2012, § 3-162; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
174:
For the purpose of this chapter, notice shall be deemed to be delivered when such notice is personally served, served upon the licensee's registered agent, or, if mailed, it must be mailed to the licensee at the address given in the latest application for the license under this article by certified mail, return receipt requested, and shall be deemed delivered on the third business day after the date of deposit in the United States mail.
(Code 2012, § 3-163; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
177:
(a) No outdoor advertising or signs promoting the sale of alcoholic beverages or the prices thereof shall be permitted on the premises of any establishment operated pursuant to a license under this article.
(b) Wholesale dealers may place wall-mounted signs on the principal building advertising the name of the company and brands sold at wholesale. Such signs must otherwise comply with city ordinances regulating signs.
(Code 2012, § 3-186; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
178:
(a) A retail consumption dealer which is an indoor commercial recreational establishment shall not sell alcoholic beverages at any time that such dealer is having a promotion or event for which it can reasonably be anticipated that in excess of fifty (50) percent of those persons attending will be under twenty-one (21) years of age.
(b) A retail consumption dealer which is an outdoor commercial recreational establishment shall not sell alcoholic beverages at any time that such dealer is having a promotion or event for which it can reasonably be anticipated that in excess of fifty (50) percent of those persons attending will be under twenty-one (21) years of age.
(Code 2012, § 3-187; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
179:
There shall be no gambling, betting, lotteries, games of chance or the operation of any scheme for hazarding money or any other thing of value on the premises of any retail consumption dealer. No retail consumption dealer shall permit in his establishment slot machines, pinball machines or similar machines which require a federal gambling stamp. Notwithstanding anything in this division to the contrary, this section shall not prohibit the sale on the premises of any retail consumption dealer of state lottery tickets, cards or games which are legally sold under the laws of the state.
(Code 2012, § 3-188; Ord. No. 147, 11-11-2002)
180:
(a) Alcoholic beverage sales can be made by a retail consumption dealer in a patio/open area type environment if the retail consumption dealer has been approved to do so by the city clerk.
(b) To obtain such approval, the patio/open area must be enclosed by a permanent structure providing for public ingress/egress only through the main structure on the premises covered by the license. The purpose of this requirement is to prevent a customer from leaving the outside sales area with an open drink container without the licensee's knowledge.
(c) The height of the enclosing structure shall be a minimum of four (4) feet above ground level. Such enclosing structure does not have to be solid, nor does it have to restrict visibility into or out of the patio/open sales area. Such enclosing structure must be permitted and approved by the engineering services department.

(a) Recomputation of tax; authority to make; basis of recomputation. If the city clerk is not satisfied with the return of the tax or the amount of the tax to be paid to the city by any person, the city clerk may cause an audit of the books and records of the licensee to be performed and may compute and determine the amount required to be paid upon the basis of any information within the city clerk's possession or that may come into the city clerk's possession. (c) Offsetting of overpayments. In making a deficiency determination, the city clerk may offset overpayments for a period against underpayments for another period, penalties and the interest on underpayments.

The notice may be served personally or by mail. If such service is made by mail, such service shall be made pursuant to section 3-163.

Except in the case of fraud, intent to evade the provisions of this article or authorized rules and regulations, or failure to make a return, every notice of a deficiency determination shall be mailed within three (3) years after the tenth day of every month following the monthly period for which the amount is proposed to be determined, or within three (3) years after the return is filed, whichever period should last expire.

(a) Security. Whenever the city clerk deems it necessary to ensure compliance with this article, he may require any person subject to such sections to deposit with him such security as the city clerk may determine. The amount of the security shall be fixed by the city clerk, but shall not be greater than twice the person's estimated average liability for the period for which he files returns, determined in such a manner as the city clerk deems proper, or ten thousand dollars ($10,000.00), whichever amount is the lesser. The amount of the security may be increased by the city clerk subject to the limitations provided in this section. The city clerk may sell the security at public auction, with the approval of the city council, if it becomes necessary to do so in order to recover any tax or any amount required to be collected, interest or penalty due. Notice of the sale may be served upon the person who deposited the security personally or by mail. If service is by mail, it shall be made in the manner prescribed for service of a notice of determined deficiency and shall be addressed to the person at his address as it appears in the records of the city clerk. Upon any sale, any surplus above the amounts due shall be returned to the person who deposited the security.
(b) Notice of delinquency to persons holding credits or property of delinquent; duty of persons so notified. If any person is delinquent in the payment of the amount required to be paid by him, or if a delinquency determination has been made against him which remains unpaid, the city clerk may, not later than three (3) years after the payment became delinquent, give notice thereof by registered mail to all persons in the city having in their possession or under their control any credits or other personal property belonging to the delinquent, or owing any debts to the delinquent. After receiving the notice, the persons so notified shall neither transfer nor make any other disposition of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession or under their control at the time they receive the notice until the city clerk consents to a transfer or disposition, or until twenty (20) days elapse after the receipt of the notice. All persons so notified shall, within five (5) days after receipt of the notice, advise the city clerk of all of the credits, other personal property or debts in their possession, under their control or owing by them.
(c) Action for tax collection. At any time within three (3) years after any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article becomes due and payable, and at any time within three (3) years after the delinquency of any tax or any amount of tax required to be collected under this article, the city clerk may bring an action in the courts of this state, any other state or of the United States in the name of city to collect the amount delinquent, together with penalties and interest, court fees, filing fees, attorney's fees and other legal fees incident thereto.
(d) Duty of successors or assignees of licensee to withhold tax from purchase money. If any licensee liable for any amount under this article sells out his business or quits the business, his successors or assigns shall withhold a sufficient amount of the purchase price to cover such amount until the former owner produces a receipt from the city clerk showing that he has been paid or a certificate stating that no amount is due.
(e) Liability for failure to withhold; certificate of notice of amount due; time to enforce successor's liability. If the purchaser of a business fails to withhold the purchase price as required, he becomes personally liable for the payment of the amount required to be withheld by him to the extent of the purchase price valued in money. Within thirty (30) days after receiving a written request from the purchaser for a certificate, the city clerk shall either issue the certificate or mail notice to the purchaser at his address, as it appears on the records of the city clerk, of the amount that must be paid as a condition of issuing the certificate. The time within which the obligation of the successor may be enforced shall begin at the time the licensee sells out his business or at the time that the determination against the licensee becomes final, whichever occurs later.
(f) Refund of tax, penalty or interest paid more than once or illegally collected. Whenever the amount of any tax, penalty or interest has been paid more than once, or has been erroneously or illegally collected or received by the city under this article, it may be offset as provided in section 3-254(c) or it may be refunded provided a verified claim in writing therefor, stating the specific grounds upon which the claim is founded, is filed with the city clerk within three (3) years from the date of payment. The claim shall be audited and shall be made on forms provided by the city clerk. If the claim is approved by the city clerk and the city council, the excess amount collected or paid may be refunded or may be credited on any amounts then due and payable from the person from whom it was collected or by whom paid, and the balance may be refunded to such person, his administrators or executors.
(g) Council may decline to issue license. The city council or its designated committee may decline to issue a license under this article when any person having any ownership interest in or control over the land or building in which the establishment to be operated pursuant to the license will be located does not meet the same character requirements as set forth in this section for the licensee.
(h) Appointment of registered agent. If a person in whose name a license under this article is issued is not a county resident, such person must appoint and continuously maintain in the county a registered agent upon whom any process, notice or demand required or permitted by law or under this article may be served. The registered agent must be a resident of the county. If the licensee is not a natural person, it will be required to appoint and maintain a registered agent in the county if it does not have in the county any agent upon whom process can legally be served for such entity under the laws of the state. The licensee shall file the name of such registered agent, along with the written consent to serve of such agent, with the city clerk.
(i) Denial of application. An application for a license under this article may be denied where it appears to the city council or its designated committee that the applicant does not have adequate financial strength, adequate financial participation in the proposed business to direct and manage its affairs, or where it appears that the applicant is intended or is likely to be a surrogate for a person who would not otherwise qualify for a license under this article.
(j) Consideration of extenuating circumstances. The city council or its designated committee, in its discretion, may consider any extenuating circumstances which may reflect favorably or unfavorably on the applicant, the application or the proposed location of the establishment. If, in the city council's or the committee's judgment, circumstances are such that issuing of a license under this article would not be in the best interest of the general public, such circumstances may be grounds for denying the application.

The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this chapter, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Animal means any member of the family "Animalis."
At-large means off of the property of the animal's owner, unless under control of the owner or within a vehicle being driven or parked on the streets or highways of the city.
Attack dog means a dog which has been trained in any manner to attack persons or animals upon command.
Cat means any animal classified as "Felis libyca domestica."
Control. An animal shall be deemed to be under control when it is controlled by a leash or other physical attachment or is within the property limits of its owner or beside a competent person and obedient to such person's command or is in a vehicle being driven or parked on the streets or highways of the city or is in the rear of a pickup or open truck and controlled by a leash or other physical attachment.
Dangerous dog means any dog that, according to the records of animal control:
(1) Inflicts a severe injury on a human without provocation on public or private property at any time after March 31, 1989; or
(2) Aggressively bites, attacks or endangers the safety of humans without provocation after the dog has been classified as a potentially dangerous dog and after the owner has been notified of such classification.
Dog means any animal classified as "Canis familiaris."
Dog control officer means an individual selected under this Code or under provisions of O.C.G.A. § 4-8-22(c) to aid in the administration and enforcement of this chapter and applicable state law.
Guard-security dog means a dog which has been trained or is used for guard and/or security purposes.
Inoculation means the administration of antirabic vaccine, approved by the board of health of the county, administered by a licensed veterinarian or other person approved and authorized by such board of health to administer inoculations.
Kennel, city, means three (3) or more dogs six (6) months or older. (See the zoning ordinance for more complete detail.)
Kennel or pound, county, means any premises designated by the animal control department for the purpose of impounding and caring for dogs and other animals found at-large in violation of this chapter.
Livestock means any animal of the equine, bovine, or swine class, including goats, sheep, mules, horses, hogs, cattle, and other grazing animals.
Owner means any person as defined in section 1-2, specifically including, but not limited to, an individual, corporation, partnership, firm, or trust owner, possessing, harboring, keeping, or having custody or control of a dog, dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog or any other animal within the city.
Potentially dangerous dog means any dog that without provocation bites a human being on public or private property at any time after March 31, 1989.
Proper enclosure means an enclosure for keeping a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog while on the owner's property securely confined indoors or in a securely enclosed and locked pen, fence, or structure suitable to prevent the entry of young children or other individuals and designed to prevent the dog from escaping. Any such pen or structure shall have secure sides and a secure top, and, if the dog is enclosed within a fence, all sides of the fence shall be of sufficient height and the bottom of the fence shall be constructed or secured in such a manner as to prevent the dog's escape either from over or from under the fence. Any such enclosure shall also provide protection from the elements for the dog. A symbol indicating a dangerous dog will be posted clearly (see section 4-42, Figure 1).
Records of an appropriate authority means records of any state, county, or municipal law enforcement agency; records of any county, or municipal animal control agency; records of any county board of health; records of any federal, state, or local court; or records of a dog control officer provided for in this chapter.
Severe injury means any physical injury that results in broken bones or disfiguring lacerations requiring multiple sutures or cosmetic surgery or a physical injury that results in death.
Vicious animal means a savagely aggressive, or dangerous, animal with a known propensity, tendency or disposition to attack unprovoked, to cause injury, or to otherwise threaten the safety of human beings.
(Code 2012, § 4-1)

(a) Prohibited. No person shall, by such person's act, omission or neglect, cause unjustifiable physical pain, suffering or death to any living animal. This section does not apply to killing of animals raised for the purpose of providing food, nor does it apply to any person who hunts wild animals in compliance with the game and fish laws of this state. Killing or injuring an animal for humane purposes or in the furtherance of medical or scientific research is justifiable.
(b) Permitted acts. No person shall perform a cruel act on any animal, nor shall any person harm, maim or kill any animal, or attempt to do so; except that a person may:
(1) Defend such person's self or property or the person or property of another from injury or damage being caused by an animal; or
(2) Kill any animal causing injury or damage to livestock or poultry.
(c) Physical abuse. It is unlawful for any person to willfully or maliciously kill, maim, disfigure, torture, beat with a stick, chain, club, or other object, mutilate, burn or scald with any substance, drive over or otherwise cruelly set upon any animal, except that reasonable force may be employed to drive off vicious or trespassing animals.
(d) Failure to care for and maintain. It is unlawful for any person to fail, refuse, or neglect to provide any animal in such person's charge or custody, as owner or otherwise, with proper food, drink, shade, care or shelter, or to carry any animal in or upon any vehicle in a cruel or inhumane manner. Any animal habitually kept outside shall be provided with a structurally sound, weatherproof enclosure, large enough to accommodate the animal.
(e) Keeping diseased or crippled animal. It is unlawful for any person to have, keep, or harbor any animal which is infected with any dangerous disease or any incurable, painfully crippling condition. The animal control department may impound such diseased or painfully crippled animal, and all such animals impounded may be disposed of humanely as soon thereafter as conveniently possible. In the case of humane disposition of such animal, the animal control department shall not be required to give any notice. This section shall not be construed to include veterinary hospitals or animals under active veterinary care.
(f) Authority of animal control department in case of animal neglect. Whenever the animal control board finds that any animal is or will be without proper care because of injury, illness, incarceration or other voluntary absence of the owner or person responsible for the care of such animal, or because of the failure, refusal or neglect of the owner or person responsible for the care of such animal to provide proper care, the animal control department may pick up such animal for protective care; and in the event of sickness or injury, the animal control department may take such action as called for to prevent undue pain and suffering, including immediate humane disposal of the animal.

(a) No person shall walk any dog in any public park except on a leash, unless the area of the park is explicitly designated as an off-leash dog area.
(b) It shall be the responsibility of any person bringing a dog into a public park to clean up any matter excreted by the dog.
(c) Leashed dogs are prohibited in the following areas of any public parks:
(1) Tennis courts.
(2) Ball fields.
(d) This section shall not apply to any guide dog especially trained for the purpose of accompanying a totally or partially blind or deaf person, or a service dog especially trained for the purpose of accompanying a physically disabled person, or a dog trained and in the possession of the city department of public safety, or any other law enforcement agency.
(e) Certain defined areas of select public parks may be designated as off-leash dog areas. These areas must be completely fenced with a double-gated entrance and exit system. For any area of a park designated as an off-leash dog area, the rules set forth below shall apply. All of the rules below shall be posted on a sign at the off-leash area. In the event that the rules are not posted, users of the area shall still be held responsible for knowing and following the rules, and may be fined or otherwise penalized for failure to abide by such rules. These rules may be augmented by the director of leisure and recreation services or his designee should he determine that additional rules are needed.
(1) All users of the off-leash area shall assume all risk and liability associated with such an area.
(2) Dog handlers are responsible for any injury or damage caused by their dogs. Each dog must be kept within sight of his owner and under voice control.
(3) Dog handlers have responsibility for watching their dog's behavior. If a dog displays aggressive behavior or fights, the handler shall be responsible for immediately controlling or removing the dog from the off-leash area.
(4) No more than three dogs per handler shall be allowed in the off-leash area at one time.
(5) Dog handlers must be sixteen (16) years of age or older.
(6) Dog handlers must carry a leash with them at all times while in the off-leash area.
(7) Dog handlers must stop their dogs from digging and are responsible for filling holes their dogs create.
(8) All dogs must wear a collar and ID tag.
(9) All dogs must be properly licensed, healthy, and have current vaccinations.
(10) No puppies under four (4) months of age are allowed.
(11) No dogs in heat are allowed.
(12) No dogs are permitted to enter with pronged collars.
(13) Any dog that barks continually must be removed or muzzled by his handler.
(14) Handlers are responsible for picking up and disposing of their dog's waste in designated receptacles.
(15) The off-leash areas have double-gated entrances. Handlers must close and latch both gates after entering or exiting the area.
(16) No children under the age of twelve (12) are allowed in the off-leash area without close adult supervision.
(17) No food or smoking is permitted within the off-leash area.
(18) No bathing of dogs is permitted within the park.
(19) Bicycling, skateboarding, rollerblading, jogging or strollers are not allowed within the off-leash area.
(20) The off-leash area may be closed in times of bad weather or for maintenance.
(21) Serious problems resulting in injury must be reported immediately to the Grovetown Department of Public Safety.
(Ord. No. 252, § 2(4-33), 7-10-2017)

(c) The notice shall be dated and shall state that the owner, within fifteen (15) days after the date shown on the notice, has the right to request a hearing on the dog control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog:
(1) The notice shall state that the hearing, if requested, shall be before the animal control board;
(2) The notice shall state that if a hearing is not requested, the dog control officer's determination that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog will become effective for all purposes under this division on a date specified in the notice, which shall be after the last day on which the owner has a right to request a hearing; and
(3) The notice shall include a form to request a hearing before the animal control board and shall provide specific instructions on mailing or delivering such request to the agency.
(d) When the animal control board receives a request for a hearing as provided in subsection (c) of this section, it shall schedule such hearing within thirty (30) days after receiving the request. The board shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of the date, time, and place of hearing, and such notice shall be mailed to the dog owner at least ten (10) days prior to the date of the hearing. At the hearing, the owner of the dog shall be given the opportunity to testify and present evidence and in addition thereto the board shall receive such other evidence and hear such other testimony as the board may find reasonably necessary to make a determination either to sustain, modify, or overrule the dog control officer's classification of the dog.
(e) Within ten (10) days after the date of the hearing, the animal control board shall notify the dog owner in writing by certified mail of its determination on the matter. If such determination is that the dog is a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog, the notice shall specify the date upon which that determination is effective.
(f) The owner of a dangerous dog or a potentially dangerous dog shall notify the dog control officer immediately upon discovery if it is on the loose, unconfined, has attacked a human, has died, or has been sold or donated. If the dog has been sold or donated, the owner shall also provide the dog control officer with the name, address, and telephone number of the new owner of the dog.
(g) The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog shall notify the dog control officer if the owner is moving from the dog control officer's jurisdiction. The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog who is a new resident of the city shall register the dog as required in this section within thirty (30) days after becoming a resident. The owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog who moves from another jurisdiction to this city shall register the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog in this city within ten (10) days after becoming a resident.
(h) Issuance of a certificate of registration or the renewal of a certificate of registration by the city does not warrant or guarantee that the requirements specified in subsections (b) and (c) of this section are maintained by the owner of a dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog on a continuous basis following the date of the issuance of the initial certificate of registration or following the date of any annual renewal of such certificate.
(i) A dog control officer is authorized to make whatever inquiry is deemed necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of this division. The chief of police shall cooperate with dog control officers in enforcing the provisions of this division.
(j) Pursuant to O.C.G.A. § 4-8-25, the dog control officer shall charge an additional fee of one hundred fifty dollars ($150.00) per year for registration of dangerous dogs and a registration fee of one hundred dollars ($100.00) per year for registration of potentially dangerous dogs. Such fees shall be in addition to all other fees normally charged for the registration of dogs. Certificates of registration shall be renewed on an annual basis. At the time of the annual renewal of a certificate of registration, a dog control officer shall require evidence from the owner or make such investigation as may be necessary to verify that the dangerous dog or potentially dangerous dog is continuing to be confined in a proper enclosure and that the owner is continuing to comply with other provisions of this division.
